text: . Global ratings agency Fitch Ratings has affirmed India’s sovereign rating at ‘BBB-‘ with a stable outlook, citing robust growth prospects, improving macroeconomic stability and strong external finances.Fitch said in a note that India’s economy remains strong, despite headwinds from the energy shock. It has projected country’s GDP growth at 6.4 percent in Financial Year 2027. The GDP forecast was lower than 7.4 percent average recorded over the previous three years, but still three times the 2 per cent median growth rate for the ‘BBB’ rating category. Fitch said India’s medium-term growth outlook remains robust, led by public capital expenditure, a recovery in private investment, and favourable demographics. The agency added that healthy corporate and bank balance sheets could support private investment over time, despite recent restraint.The ratings agency said it expects India’s resilience to external shocks to continue, although uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran conflict poses residual risks given the country’s position as a large net energy importer. Fitch expects the RBI to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent later this year, citing risks of second-round effects from higher energy prices and El Nino conditions.

. India continued its impressive medal-winning run at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria. After securing 17 medals on the opening day on Monday, Indian fencers added more Medals to the country’s tally.Karan Singh and Sherjin Shanthimol clinched gold medals for India in the senior men’s events last night. In the men’s Sabre final, Karan Singh staged a remarkable comeback against Australia’s Yoongi Shim. Trailing 7-11, Karan fought back strongly to win the bout 15-12 and claim the gold medal. In the men’s Epee final, Sherjin Shanthimol defeated second-seeded South African fencer Pieter Kruger 15-6 in a comfortable victory to secure the top spot.India also won a bronze medal in the senior men’s Foil event, with Tejas Patil finishing on the podium in a field featuring several renowned international fencers.Indian women fencers put up another dominant performance in the senior women’s Epee event, winning three medals. Tanishka Khatri clinched the gold, while her compatriot Khushi Dabhade took the silver. Prachi Lohan added a bronze medal to India’s tally, sharing the third position with Australia’s Harrison Asley.In the individual Sabre event, Indian women won three medals. Aakhari secured the silver medal, finishing behind England’s Brierley, while Shruti Joshi and Jefarlin won bronze medals.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to move the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 for consideration and passing in Rajya Sabha today to alter the name of Kerala. In Lok Sabha, Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 to be tabled for consideration and passing.The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill seeks to change the name of the state of Kerala to Keralam in the First Schedule of the Constitution. A resolution in this regard was passed by the Kerala Legislative Assembly in June 2024. The resolution stated that while the State is known as Keralam in Malayalam, its name is recorded as Kerala in the First Schedule of the Constitution.Meanwhile, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 aims to amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. The bill aims to make India’s mining sector more efficient, investment-friendly and well equipped to fulfill the country’s growing demand for critical minerals.

. The FIH Hockey Men’s and Women’s World Cup 2026 will feature a revamped competition structure, with the traditional quarterfinal stage scrapped and the top two teams from each of the two crossover pools advancing directly to the semi-finals. Belgium and the Netherlands jointly host the tournament from August 15 to 30. The new format means teams will have little margin for error from the outset, with results from the opening pool stage potentially carrying over into the next phase. India’s men have been drawn alongside England, Pakistan and Wales in Pool D, while the Indian women will face China, England and South Africa in their Pool D campaign.The tournament will begin with the 16 teams in each competition split across four pools of four. From August 15 to 20, every team will play three matches against the other sides in its pool, with the final standings determining the composition of the next phase. The top two teams from Pools A and D will move into Pool E, while the leading two teams from Pools B and C will form Pool F. The top two finishers from Pool E and Pool F will advance directly to the last four. The women’s tournament will conclude in the Netherlands on August 29, with the bronze-medal match followed by the final. The men’s World Cup will conclude in Belgium a day later, on August 30, with its bronze-medal match and final.

. India’s Ambassador to Israel, J.P. Singh, met the Head of MASHAV, Israel’s Agency for International Development Cooperation, Eynat Shlein, in Jerusalem to discuss ways to further expand and deepen the India-Israel development partnership through MASHAV. The discussions covered cooperation in several areas, including Centres of Excellence in agriculture, capacity building in agriculture and water management, and new avenues of cooperation in aquaculture. The Indian Embassy in Israel said the two sides also exchanged views on further strengthening the partnership.MASHAV, under Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was established to share Israeli knowledge, expertise and technologies with other countries to help them address development challenges.

. In the World Athletics U20 Championships, India enjoyed a historic day in Eugene, USA, with Basant Kumar Meghwal and Shahnavaz Khan becoming the first Indians to win medals in the high jump and long jump at the championships. Basant Kumar Meghwal, the reigning Asian U20 champion, won silver in the men’s high jump with a personal best clearance of 2.21 metres. Shahnavaz Khan claimed bronze in the men’s long jump with a best effort of 7.84 metres.Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the high jump gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took bronze. The two medals took India’s tally at the championships to three. India have now equalled their medal haul from the 2021 and 2022 editions.

. Indian weightlifter Maharajan Arumugapandian clinched the silver medal in the men’s 65 kg category at the Asian Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan today.Maharajan produced a new personal best total of 285 kilograms, lifting 128 kg in the snatch and 157 kg in the clean and jerk to secure silver. Vietnam’s Hoang Thach claimed the gold medal with a total lift of 291 kilograms, finishing six kilograms ahead of Maharajan.

. The two-day BRICS WAVES Bazaar, a premier international marketplace for the creative economy began in Mumbai today. The event, being held under India’s BRICS Presidency brings together over 500 delegates from BRICS members and partners from 21 countries with an aim to create stronger pathways for collaboration across film, television, animation, VFX, gaming, music, digital media and emerging content formats.Information and Broadcasting Secretary, Mr. Chanchal Kumar said WAVES Bazaar seeks to become a platform for the global creative economy where projects are discovered, partnerships are initiated, co-productions are discussed and new markets are opened. Delivering the keynote address in the opening ceremony, Maharashtra’s Minister of Electronics, IT, AI and Culture, Adv. Ashish Shelar said the BRICS WAVES Bazaar is a high-level, curated confluence designed to shape the future of the global creative economy. The event features high-level conferences, keynote addresses, panel discussions, business networking sessions, and curated Business-to-Business meetings.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 1.4 per cent up at 1,52,803 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver rose 1.7 per cent to 2,35,352 rupees per kilogram

. The Fourth Session of the India-Namibia Joint Trade Committee (JTC) concluded in New Delhi today. The session which began yesterday, was led by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Amit Kumar from the Indian side while the Namibian delegation was led by the Namibian Executive Director, Ministry of International Relations and Trade Ndiitah Nghipondoka-Robiati. The agreed minutes of the Session were signed by the two Co-Chairs today.The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that during the meeting, both sides underlined the need to move bilateral trade beyond a raw-material-based composition towards value addition within Namibia, and to translate discussions into concrete mechanisms with defined timelines and assigned responsibilities. The Ministry added that the bilateral merchandise trade between India and Namibia rose to over 592 million dollars in 2025-26 from 568 million dollars in 2024-25.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will release the autobiography of former President Ram Nath Kovind, titled “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”, in New Delhi today. The Prime Minister will also address a gathering on the occasion.The autobiography offers a deeply personal account of former President Ram Nath Kovind’s life journey, tracing his experiences, struggles and achievements from his early years to his distinguished public life and eventual service as the 14th President of India. The book provides insights into the values, experiences and circumstances that shaped his journey and public service.The release of the autobiography by the Prime Minister will mark a significant occasion celebrating the life and contributions of one of India’s most distinguished public figures.

. A U.S. federal court has dismissed criminal charges against Indian businessman Gautam Adani in an alleged fraud and bribery case. Brooklyn-based U.S. District Judge Nicholas Garaufis approved a request by federal prosecutors to drop the case. However, the judge expressed concern over the Justice Department’s decision to abandon the prosecution.The judge had sought clarification on the reasons for dropping the charges, including whether Mr Adani’s November 2024 pledge to invest 10 billion dollars in the United States had influenced the decision. Judge Garaufis said he was satisfied that the investment pledge had not played a role in the Justice Department’s decision. He also noted that the role of courts in reviewing prosecutors’ decisions to drop federal criminal charges is limited.Reacting to the court’s decision, Gautam Adani said he welcomed it with humility and deep respect for the judicial process. He said that throughout the challenging period, his faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering. Mr Adani expressed gratitude to those who continued to have faith in him, the legal system and India’s capacity for justice. He said the Adani Group would remain committed to nation-building, creating lasting value and serving a larger purpose.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 15 paise to end at 95 rupees and 44 paise against the US dollar.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.

. In a significant initiative to encourage and promote emerging filmmaking talent from the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) has announced the IFFJK Emerging Filmmakers Competition 2026, as part of the scheduled 1st International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK). Registrations for the competition has commenced from today. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the competition is exclusively open to aspiring filmmakers from J&K and aims to provide a prestigious platform for young storytellers to showcase their creativity, cinematic vision and technical skills through original short films.The aspiring and emerging filmmakers are invited to submit original short films with a maximum duration of five minutes and the last date for submission is August 26. The applicants must be between 18 and 39 years of age as on September 1, 2026, and possess a valid domicile certificate of J&K. The competition is being organised around the theme “Rang-e-Cinema: Frames of a New Jammu & Kashmir”, reflecting the evolving cultural, social and creative narratives of the region while encouraging youth to present compelling stories through the medium of cinema. Interested filmmakers and cinematographers are advised to register by visiting the official IFFJK website www.iffjk.org and the detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria and the registration process are also available on this website for ease of aspirants. DIPR urges aspiring filmmakers from across J&K to seize this opportunity and contribute towards strengthening the Union Territory’s growing film culture through innovative and impactful storytelling.

. India’s medal tally rises to three at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships in the United States. India’s Basant Kumar Meghwal wins a silver in the high jump, while Shahnavaz Khan wins a bronze in the long jump today. In the men’s high jump, 19-year-old Meghwal cleared his personal best of 2.21 metres to win a silver medal. He became the first Indian to win a medal in the high jump at the World U-20 Championships. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took the bronze.In the men’s long jump, Shahnavaz clinched bronze with a best effort of 7.84 metres. The 18-year-old produced his best jump in his third attempt. Italy’s Daniele Inzoli won the gold medal with a jump of 7.97 metres, while Australia’s Mason McGroder took silver with a personal best of 7.96 metres. Earlier, in the javelin throw, Ashish Yadav won silver and became the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to win at the World Athletics U20 Championships. Yadav produced his best throw of 74.09 metres in the third round yesterday.

. The death toll from Congo’s Ebola outbreak has surpassed two thousand mark. According to government data released last night, the outbreak has so far recorded, 4,381 confirmed cases, including 2.011 deaths, while 704 patients remain in admission and isolation facilities. Health authorities are struggling to reach remote areas affected by the outbreak because of rebel conflict, poor road conditions and work stoppages linked to payment disputes. The outbreak is also unusual because the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for it currently has no approved vaccines or treatments.  The Ebola outbreak is already become the second-largest in history, only behind the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak that recorded more than 28,000 cases, including over 11,000 deaths

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. NSE Indices Limited has announced the replacement of stocks in various indices, including the NIFTY 50, as part of its semi-annual review. According to the Exchange, BSE Limited will be included in the NIFTY 50, replacing Wipro Limited. The changes will take effect on September 30, 2026. NSE Indices has also announced changes across several other broad-market, sectoral, and thematic indices as part of the periodic review.

. Former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad and several former officials have been sentenced to death by a Syrian court for crimes against humanity, premeditated murder and torture. According to Syria’s state news agency, Judge Fakhr al-Din al-Aryan said, Assad was convicted for his role as the country’s highest decision-maker and for ordering state institutions to carry out the violations. Assad’s cousin, Atef Najib, and several other former officials were also handed death sentences. Assad’s government collapsed on December 8, 2024, following a 12-day offensive led by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and allied militant groups. Assad and his family subsequently fled to Moscow after his government collapsed in Syria.

. The Supreme Court has asked the 19 remaining States and Union Territories to consider declaring cancer a “notifiable disease” to facilitate early detection and ensure proper care of patients. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, issued the direction yesterday. The court was informed that 17 of the 36 States and Union Territories have already notified cancer as a notifiable disease, following recommendations made by a Parliamentary Standing Committee.The Supreme Court had earlier issued notices to the Centre and all States and Union Territories on a Public Interest Litigation-PIL seeking a direction to declare cancer a notifiable disease across the country.The Centre told the court that health is a State subject and pointed out that 17 States have already notified cancer. The court directed the remaining States and Union Territories to consider the recommendations and take appropriate decisions. It also directed them to file compliance affidavits.The Supreme Court has also sought measures for implementing cancer screening across the country.

. In Jammu and Kashmir, a mega Tiranga rally was held today near the Line of Control in Teetwal, Karnah area of Kupwara district. A 1,200-metre-long National Flag was carried during the rally, which saw participation from school students, teachers, ex-servicemen, civil and police officials, civil society members and local residents.The participants marched along the route carrying the Tricolour and raised patriotic slogans.Meanwhile, two major bike and bicycle rallies were held from Sports Stadium Budgam as part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga campaign, with hundreds of bikers and cyclists participating from across the district.

. Karkkidaka Vavu Bali, the traditional ritual of paying homage to departed ancestors, is being performed today at various temples across Keralam.Karkkidaka Vavu Bali has begun in the early hours across Keralam. The rituals began between 3:30 a.m. and 5 a.m. at most temples.The new moon day in the Malayalam month of Karkkidakam is considered the most sacred day in Hindu tradition for performing rites for departed souls.Various Devaswom boards and temples have made extensive preparations for devotees. Additional security arrangements have been made along riverbanks and coastal areas in view of the rains.

. The United States will soon make online applications mandatory for several immigration benefits, including green cards, citizenship and asylum, in a move aimed at improving efficiency and reducing operational costs. The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) said in a new rule published in the Federal Register that forms which have been available for electronic filing for at least 180 days will be required to be submitted online.The rule will also establish a process to make immigration forms available exclusively online, after providing applicants with at least 60 days’ notice. The changes could affect a wide range of immigration benefits, including green card applications and renewals, family-based petitions, citizenship applications, asylum claims, employment authorisation and Temporary Protected Status filings.Applicants will generally be required to use a USCIS online account. They can either complete the form online or upload a PDF of the completed form along with supporting documents. The USCIS said the move is intended to streamline the immigration application process and lower administrative costs.

Inflows into the Indian Inflows into the Indian equity mutual funds fell by 14.8 per cent to 24,697 crore rupees in July, fell by 14.8 per cent to 24,697 crore rupees in July, compared with 28,973 crore rupees in June. According to data released by the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) contributions stood at 31,961 crore rupees in July, marking a marginal increase from June.Among the equity fund categories, Small-cap funds attracted the highest inflows in July, garnering more than 7,700 crore rupees. They were followed by Mid-cap funds, flexi-cap funds, and Multi-cap funds. However, large-cap and Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) funds witnessed net outflows during the period. The Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) inflow dipped to 1,559 crore rupees last month on a sequential basis. Meanwhile, the trend reversed in Debt funds which witnessed net inflows of 1 lakh 87 thousand 511 crore rupees last month as compared with the outflows recorded in previous months. Within debt-oriented schemes, liquid funds attracted the highest net inflow of over 1 lakh 19 thousand crore rupees.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has relaxed the timelines for municipalities with listed municipal debt securities under its regulations to submit financial results to stock exchanges.Under the revised framework issued yesterday, listed municipalities will now have to submit half-yearly unaudited financial results within 60 days of the first half-year, compared with the earlier 45-day deadline. Annual audited financial results will have to be submitted within 90 days from the end of the financial year along with the audit report, against the earlier 60 days. The regulator said timelines have been relaxed considering the practical challenges faced by municipalities during data collection, interdepartmental coordination and meeting disclosure requirements. The changes form part of operational measures specified by Sebi through a circular amending the framework for issue of listing of municipal debt securities.SEBI has also introduced a two-step escrow account mechanism for issuers that are pooled finance vehicles or special purpose vehicles set up under the Government’s Pooled Finance Development Fund Scheme. Besides, it has also specified face value requirements for privately placed municipal debt securities.

. Parliament has passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, with the Rajya Sabha approving it today. Lok Sabha has already passed the bill. When the House met at 2:00 PM after the second adjournment, Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal moved the Bill. It aims to improve efficiency, ensure independence, transparency, and uniformity in the qualifications, appointment, and service of Chairpersons and Members of various Tribunals, as well as the administration and functioning of the Tribunals. The legislation also proposes to establish a National Tribunals Commission.Replying to discussion on the bill, Mr Meghwal said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government initiated the process of rationalisation of tribunals in 2015. He said, the Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026 has been brought to establish a modern, independent, and uniform tribunal ecosystem. Mr Meghwal highlighted that the bill is aimed at strengthening governance, institutional independence, transparency, and efficiency.The Minister said, the new bill has a provision to establish the National Tribunals Commission it will be chaired by a former Judge of the Supreme Court or a former Chief Justice of a High Court. Mr Meghwal said that this reform is an important milestone towards promoting ease of justice, ease of doing business and the adoption of global best practices. The Minister said, it will further strengthen India’s legal and institutional architecture and advance the government’s collective commitment to ensuring accessible, timely and speedy justice. He said, the new bill will further strengthen the resolve of making India a developed nation by 2047.Earlier, participating in the bill, Subhash Barala of BJP supported the bill, saying that the bill is not only intended to bring changes in the administrative functioning of the tribunals but also intended to ensure fair and speedy justice. He said, the reforms that took place in the country in the last 11 years will also get a boost through this legislation. Mr Barala informed that once the legislation becomes an Act, the tribunal system will be further strengthened and speedy resolution of disputes will be ensured.Dr Sasmit Patra of BJD supported the bill saying that the tribunal reform is not about administrative reform alone as it is a question of judicial architecture. He urged the government to include the National Company Law Tribunal into this legislation apart from the 16 tribunals as this will help strengthen the adjudication fabric of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.Tiruchi Siva of DMK said the Bill seeks to repeal and replace the Tribunals Reforms Act 2021. He said that the government has brought this new bill because certain provision of this Act was struck down by the Supreme Court. Mr Siva said the legislation proposes to establish a National Tribunals Commission.Mahesh Kewat of BJP said that this bill is a historic and revolutionary step towards making the country’s justice system more streamlined, transparent, speedy and accountable. He said, the basic objective behind the establishment of tribunals was to ensure that disputes in specialised areas such as taxation, environment, labour and administrative matters could be resolved expeditiously.Besides other members including S Reddy of YSRCP, I. S Inbadurai of AIADMK, Rajendra Hiralal Jain of NCP and Bhashyam Rama Krishna of TDP also participated in the discussion.After passing the bill, the House took up special mention in which various members raised the issues of public importance. The Chair adjourned the House for the day after completing its business to meet again at 11:00 AM tomorrow.

. India today reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India and nothing can change this indisputable reality. Briefing the media in New Delhi today, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that in matters relating to the border areas, India always emphasized in discussions with China that it considers these issues as most serious. He said that the maintenance of peace and tranquility in these areas is of the utmost importance for the country.The spokesperson said this was also reiterated at the recently held 36th Meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China border affairs. At this meeting, the two sides engaged in frank discussions and reviewed the situation along the Line of Actual Control. The Indian side again underlined that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations. Both sides agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.Replying to another query, Mr Jaiswal highlighted that human rights violations being committed in Pakistan occupied Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the neighbouring country. He called upon the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for its misdeeds, abuses and gross violations of human rights.Replying to a query on defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, the spokesperson said India continue to closely follow developments in the West Asia conflict. He said that as far as this agreement is concerned, New Delhi is examining its implications both from the perspective of India’s national security and considerations of regional peace and stability. He stated that India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard.On NSA Ajit Doval meeting with US Ambassador Sergio Gor, Mr Jaiswal said they met yesterday as well as today. He added that these were occasions for both sides to discuss the comprehensive global strategic partnership that India and the US share. He said both sides remain committed to further strengthening of ties in areas of trade, defence, energy security, critical missiles, and other such areas.On Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi meeting Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Mr Jaiswal said India has extended an invitation for a bilateral visit as well as for the BRICS outreach session which will be held in Delhi.

. Sagnik Roy and Sayantan Kushari won the gold medal in the Under-31 Pairs at the 9th World Youth Transnational Championships in Hefei, China, yesterday. In the first elimination round, 34 pairs competed and the top 14 advanced to Flight A, including the Indian duo. They then competed in a round-robin format, with Sagnik and Sayantan finishing on top with 377.67 match points. M Fereneca and F Katusich of Croatia finished second with 357.78 match points, while China’s J Han and Z Wang took the third spot with 335.92 match points.

. The government has said that more than one crore 73  lakh e-Passports have been issued so far in India and abroad. In a written reply in Rajya Sabha today, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said that currently, all Regional Passport Offices, Passport Seva Kendras and Post Office Passport Seva Kendras in India and all the Indian Missions abroad are issuing e-Passports. He informed that the e-Passport was launched in May last year. Mr Singh said that the Passport Seva Programme provided comprehensive digital platforms. This includes the Passport Seva Portal, Passport Seva Mobile Apps and a centralised citizen service call centre, enabling applicants to access information, track application status and obtain responses to routine queries without visiting Regional Passport Offices. The Minister said, these digital initiatives have substantially reduced the need for physical visits for administrative enquiries while improving accessibility, convenience and service delivery.

. The Income Tax Department, as of the 10th of this month, has collected over 8.11 lakh crore rupees net direct tax for the financial year 2026-27 so far. It is 23.09 percent higher growth as compared to the financial year 2025-2026 during the same period. The collection includes corporate tax of over 2.70 lakh crore rupees and non-corporate tax of 5.07 lakh crore rupees.The department has also issued refunds of over one lakh 43 thousand crore rupees. The gross direct collection has recorded a significant growth of over 19 per cent, amounting to more than nine lakh 54 thousand crore rupees.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall over East Rajasthan, Madhya Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand and Gangetic West Bengal today. The Met department has predicted heavy rainfall over North eastern parts of country, Sikkim, Sub Himalayan West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, West Madhya Pradesh, West Rajasthan, Gujarat, Konkan, Goa, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir along with and Andaman and Nicobar Islands for the next two three days.According to IMD, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are likely to experience thunderstorm accompanied with lightning and gusty winds till tomorrow. Similar conditions are expected to prevail over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, and Uttarakhand till Saturday.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. The Reserve Bank of India Governor has called on Indian banks to adopt Artificial Intelligence with a clear focus on innovation, accountability and customer trust. Addressing the 2026 edition of FIBAC in Mumbai, the RBI Governor said AI could transform Indian banking by improving credit delivery, customer service, financial inclusion, operational efficiency and fraud detection.At the same time, the Governor cautioned banks about risks including opaque “black box” models, algorithmic bias, concentration of technology providers, data privacy, cyber vulnerabilities and excessive dependence on AI-driven decisions.The Governor urged banks to maintain an inventory of AI systems, establish board-approved AI governance policies, stress-test AI models and ensure meaningful human oversight. The Governor reiterated that the RBI chooses a principles-based and proportionate approach over a rigid, prescriptive one, as AI capabilities and risks will differ across large and small banks.

. India has made a strong start at the U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria, winning 17 medals, including 4 gold, on the opening day. The Indian contingent has secured 4 gold, 4 silver and 9 bronze medals at the championship, which began on Sunday. Indian fencers reached the podium in all 6 individual events across the Sabre, Foil and Epee disciplines.In the men’s Sabre event, Nikhil Wagh won the gold medal, while Lakshay Badser secured silver. Ashwini Arya and Laishram Moramba bagged bronze medals. In men’s Foil, Tejas Patil won silver and Hemash Sanasam secured bronze. In men’s Epee, Lokesh Vemani claimed silver, while Shaurya Ashwini and Godwin Anbkess won bronze.In the women’s events, Joys Ashita clinched gold in Foil, with teammate Kanaglakshmi winning silver. Prachi Lohan won gold in women’s Epee, while Nivedhya Nair and Anupriya secured bronze medals. . Hungary’s parliament today elected former Supreme Court chief Andras Baka as the country’s next President. Baka, who will serve in the largely ceremonial role, was elected with the support of members of the governing centre-right Tisza party. Lawmakers from the opposition Fidesz party boycotted the vote and did not take part in the election. This decision marks Prime Minister Peter Magyar’s symbolic step to dismantle entrenched power structures built under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban.

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha produced a superb comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026, beating China’s Han Qian Xi in the women’s singles final this morning. The Assam shuttler recovered from losing the opening game to prevail 14-21, 21-14, and 21-14 in 53 minutes and claim her first BWF title. Earlier, Ashmita reached the final after defeating fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal yesterday. While Han outplayed South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, and 21-14 in the other semifinal to advance to the final. Ashmita Chaliha had won the gold medal at the 2024 Asia Team Championships. At the 2019 South Asian Games, she had secured gold medals in both the women’s singles and team events.
